spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled 7 to 12, subdivided into halves, with two red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Integer ticks at 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12; half-unit subdivision ticks; points at 7.5 and 10.5.
spec.answerVisibility: Marked points are permanent givens; their numerical answers appear only in answer fields.

answer.worked:
Each whole is divided into two equal intervals. The points are halfway between $7$ and $8$, and between $10$ and $11$.

The numbers, from left to right, are $7\frac{1}{2}$ and $10\frac{1}{2}$.

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled 0 to 5, subdivided into thirds, with three red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Every integer and third-unit subdivision tick is retained. Points are at 1+2/3, 2+1/3 and 4+2/3.
spec.answerVisibility: The numerical values of the marked points are withheld from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $\frac{1}{3}$. Count the intervals after the preceding whole number:

$$\begin{align*}1+\frac{2}{3}&=1\frac{2}{3}\\2+\frac{1}{3}&=2\frac{1}{3}\\4+\frac{2}{3}&=4\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled 22 to 26 with fifth-unit subdivisions, continuing beyond 26, and four red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Fifth-unit ticks extend through 26.8. Marked points are 23+1/5, 24+2/5, 25+4/5 and 26+1/5.
spec.answerVisibility: All ticks, integer labels and marked points are visible; point values are answer-only.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $\frac{1}{5}$. Count from the preceding whole number:

$$\begin{align*}23+\frac{1}{5}&=23\frac{1}{5}\\24+\frac{2}{5}&=24\frac{2}{5}\\25+\frac{4}{5}&=25\frac{4}{5}\\26+\frac{1}{5}&=26\frac{1}{5}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled −3, −2, −1 and 0, subdivided into thirds, with four red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Points lie at −7/3, −5/3, −2/3 and −1/3, in left-to-right order.
spec.answerVisibility: Negative integer labels and all marked points remain visible; the requested values appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $\frac{1}{3}$. Moving right increases the value:

$$\begin{align*}-3+\frac{2}{3}&=-2\frac{1}{3}\\-2+\frac{1}{3}&=-1\frac{2}{3}\\-1+\frac{1}{3}&=-\frac{2}{3}\\-1+\frac{2}{3}&=-\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$$

A leading minus applies to the whole mixed numeral: $-2\frac{1}{3}=-(2+\frac{1}{3})$.

content.prompt: Convert these mixed numbers to improper fractions.

spec.description: Three circles in one row, each divided into eight equal sectors; two whole circles and five sectors of the third are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Sixteen eighths plus five eighths represent twenty-one eighths.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied shading is visible; the numerator response remains blank.

answer.worked:
Each whole contains 8 eighths. The two wholes contain 16 eighths; the remaining circle contributes 5 eighths.
$$\begin{aligned}2\frac{5}{8}&=\frac{16+5}{8}\\2\frac{5}{8}&=\frac{21}{8}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: An unpartitioned shaded whole circle followed by a circle divided into three equal sectors with the right and bottom sectors shaded.
spec.mathematics: Three thirds in the whole plus two thirds give five thirds.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given mixed-number model is visible.

answer.worked:
Split the whole into 3 thirds. Count these and the 2 shaded thirds.
$$\begin{aligned}1\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{3+2}{3}\\1\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Two squares side by side; the first is wholly shaded and the second has diagonal partitions with its right-hand triangular quarter shaded.
spec.mathematics: Four quarters plus one quarter give five quarters.
spec.answerVisibility: The given model is visible without a completed answer.

answer.worked:
Split the whole square into 4 quarters. Count these and the shaded quarter.
$$\begin{aligned}1\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{4+1}{4}\\1\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Four upright triangles in a row; three whole shaded triangles and a final triangle split into three equal-area regions with its left and bottom regions shaded.
spec.mathematics: Nine thirds plus two thirds give eleven thirds.
spec.answerVisibility: Partitions of the three wholes are left for the taught conversion method.

answer.worked:
Split each whole triangle into 3 thirds. The three wholes contain 9 thirds; count the 2 remaining shaded thirds.
$$\begin{aligned}3\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{9+2}{3}\\3\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Three pentagons with a vertex uppermost; two are wholly shaded and the third has five centre-to-vertex regions with its three left and bottom regions shaded.
spec.mathematics: Ten fifths plus three fifths give thirteen fifths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given mixed-number model is visible.

answer.worked:
Split each whole pentagon into 5 fifths. The two wholes contain 10 fifths; count the 3 remaining shaded fifths.
$$\begin{aligned}2\frac{3}{5}&=\frac{10+3}{5}\\2\frac{3}{5}&=\frac{13}{5}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Two heptagons; the first is wholly shaded without partitions and the second is divided into seven centre-to-vertex regions with its lower-right region unshaded.
spec.mathematics: Seven sevenths plus six sevenths give thirteen sevenths.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied mixed-number shading is visible without a completed response.

answer.worked:
Split the whole heptagon into 7 sevenths. Count these and the 6 remaining shaded sevenths.
$$\begin{aligned}1\frac{6}{7}&=\frac{7+6}{7}\\1\frac{6}{7}&=\frac{13}{7}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Three fully shaded circles in a horizontal row, each split into two halves by a horizontal diameter.
spec.mathematics: The six shaded halves represent three wholes.
spec.answerVisibility: The numerator of the supplied denominator-2 scaffold is blank.

answer.worked:
Each whole contains 2 halves. Count all 6 shaded halves.
$$3=\frac{6}{2}$$

spec.description: Five fully shaded hexagons, each partitioned into six triangular regions; three across the top and two centred below.

Each whole contains 6 sixths. The five hexagons contain 30 shaded sixths.

answer.worked:
Group four quarters into one whole. Three quarters remain.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{7}{4}&=\frac{4}{4}+\frac{3}{4}\\\frac{7}{4}&=1\frac{3}{4}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Group the thirds into two groups of three. Two thirds remain.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{8}{3}&=\frac{3}{3}+\frac{3}{3}+\frac{2}{3}\\\frac{8}{3}&=2\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Group the halves into three pairs. There are three wholes and no leftover parts.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{6}{2}&=\frac{2}{2}+\frac{2}{2}+\frac{2}{2}\\\frac{6}{2}&=3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{12}{4}&=\frac{4}{4}+\frac{4}{4}+\frac{4}{4}\\\frac{12}{4}&=3\end{align*}$$

Two wholes contain six thirds. One more third gives seven thirds.

Two wholes contain eight quarters. One more quarter gives nine quarters.

$$\frac{7}{3}=2\frac{1}{3}$$

The point $1\frac{3}{4}$ represents seven quarters: four quarters make one whole, with three quarters left over.
$$\frac{7}{4}=1\frac{3}{4}$$

One whole contains three thirds. Two more thirds give five thirds.
$$\frac{5}{3}=1\frac{2}{3}$$

Six quarters make one whole with two quarters left over. Two quarters equal one half.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{6}{4}&=1\frac{2}{4}\\\frac{6}{4}&=1\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$

Group three of the four thirds into one whole. One third remains.
$$\frac{4}{3}=1\frac{1}{3}$$

Two wholes contain eight quarters. Three more quarters give eleven quarters.
$$\frac{11}{4}=2\frac{3}{4}$$

$$\begin{align*}1\frac{2}{7}+\frac{2}{7}&=1\frac{4}{7}\\1\frac{6}{7}+\frac{2}{7}&=2\frac{1}{7}\\2\frac{5}{7}+\frac{2}{7}&=3\\3\frac{2}{7}+\frac{2}{7}&=3\frac{4}{7}\\3\frac{4}{7}+\frac{2}{7}&=3\frac{6}{7}\end{align*}$$

Add $\frac{3}{5}$ each time; five fifths make one whole.
$$\begin{align*}1\frac{4}{5}+\frac{3}{5}&=2\frac{2}{5}\\3\frac{3}{5}+\frac{3}{5}&=4\frac{1}{5}\\4\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{5}&=4\frac{4}{5}\\5\frac{2}{5}+\frac{3}{5}&=6\\6\frac{3}{5}+\frac{3}{5}&=7\frac{1}{5}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: A fully simplified mixed numeral between 2 and 3 is written as an improper fraction with a numerator of 17. List all the possible mixed numerals matching this description.

answer.worked:
For $\frac{17}{d}$ to lie between $2$ and $3$, the denominator must be greater than $\frac{17}{3}$ and less than $\frac{17}{2}$. The possible integer denominators are $6$, $7$ and $8$.

Dividing $17$ by each denominator gives:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{17}{6}&=2\frac{5}{6}\\\frac{17}{7}&=2\frac{3}{7}\\\frac{17}{8}&=2\frac{1}{8}\end{align*}$$
Each fractional part is fully simplified, so these are all the possible mixed numerals.

For terminating decimals, use equivalent fractions with a denominator that is a power of $10$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{5}{10}=0.5\\\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{25}{100}=0.25\\\frac{1}{5}&=\frac{2}{10}=0.2\\\frac{1}{8}&=\frac{125}{1000}=0.125\\\frac{1}{10}&=0.1\end{align*}$$
For the other fractions, divide the numerator by the denominator. The repeating digits are shown by a bar.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{3}&=0.333\ldots=0.\overline{3}\\\frac{1}{6}&=0.1666\ldots=0.1\overline{6}\\\frac{1}{7}&=0.142857142857\ldots=0.\overline{142857}\\\frac{1}{9}&=0.111\ldots=0.\overline{1}\end{align*}$$

sourceAtom.label: Identify whether a number is rational or irrational

content.prompt: Use a calculator to write decimal representations of these numbers. Keep rational decimal representations exact, using recurring notation where needed, and give irrational decimal approximations to 2 decimal places. Use the original number and the definitions of rational and irrational numbers to decide which classification to circle; a finite calculator display alone cannot establish whether a decimal terminates or recurs. Circle Rational or Irrational for each number.

answer.worked: $\frac{1}{3}=0.333\ldots=0.\dot{3}$. It is a fraction of integers with a nonzero denominator, so it is rational.
$3=3.0=\frac{3}{1}$. Its decimal terminates, so it is rational.
$0.3=\frac{3}{10}$. It is a terminating decimal, so it is rational.
$0.\dot{3}=0.333\ldots=\frac{1}{3}$. The digit $3$ repeats, so this recurring decimal is rational.
$\sqrt{3}\approx1.732050808\approx1.73$ to 2 decimal places. Since $3$ is not a perfect square, $\sqrt{3}$ is irrational; its decimal is non-terminating and non-recurring.
$\sqrt{9}=3=3.0$. Its decimal terminates, so it is rational.
$0.25=\frac{25}{100}=\frac{1}{4}$. It is a terminating decimal, so it is rational.
$25\%=\frac{25}{100}=0.25$. Its decimal terminates, so it is rational.
$\sqrt{4}=2=2.0$. Its decimal terminates, so it is rational.
$\sqrt{5}\approx2.236067977\approx2.24$ to 2 decimal places. Since $5$ is not a perfect square, $\sqrt{5}$ is irrational; its decimal is non-terminating and non-recurring.
$\sqrt{5}+1\approx3.236067977\approx3.24$ to 2 decimal places. Adding $1$ to $\sqrt{5}$ changes only the integer part; its decimal remains non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational.

$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\approx0.707106781\approx0.71$ to 2 decimal places. Dividing the irrational number $\sqrt{2}$ by the nonzero rational number $2$ gives an irrational number, with a non-terminating, non-recurring decimal.

$2\sqrt{2}\approx2.828427125\approx2.83$ to 2 decimal places. Multiplying the irrational number $\sqrt{2}$ by the nonzero rational number $2$ gives an irrational number, with a non-terminating, non-recurring decimal.
$\pi\approx3.141592654\approx3.14$ to 2 decimal places. The decimal expansion of $\pi$ is non-terminating and non-recurring, so $\pi$ is irrational.
$-\frac{22.5}{7}=-\frac{45}{14}=-3.214285714285\ldots=-3.2\overline{142857}$. It can be written as a fraction of integers with a nonzero denominator, so it is rational.
$3.\overline{14}=3.141414\ldots$. The block $14$ repeats, so this recurring decimal is rational.

answer.worked:
$\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{3}$, $\sqrt{5}$ and $\sqrt{7}$ are irrational because their radicands are not perfect squares. Multiplying $\sqrt{7}$ by $3$ or taking the negative of $\sqrt{3}$ preserves irrationality.

The irrational numbers are $\sqrt{2},\ \sqrt{3},\ \sqrt{5},\ 3\sqrt{7},\ -\sqrt{3}$.

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{4}&=2\\2\sqrt{100}&=2\times10\\&=20\\-\sqrt{25}&=-5\end{align*}$$
These values are integers, so each can be written as a fraction with denominator $1$. The rational numbers are $\sqrt{4},\ 2\sqrt{100},\ -\sqrt{25}$.

2. Simplify the fraction.
